title: Simulation of the Skip Statement
statement: For every compiler setting $S$, natural number $d$, and state $\sigma$, the skip statement simulates execution from $\sigma$ to itself with cost zero. For every admissible initial machine placement and memory encoding, the compiled code reaches its endpoint within the corresponding machine-step bound, with the memory still encoding $\sigma$ and unchanged outside writable addresses.
hypotheses_covered: For the simulation conclusion: initial frame relation, valid stack position, code located at the position and ending before the dispatcher, sufficient width, bounded source state, and sufficient stack room
replaced:
